DEL-03-02 exists to make the harness turn lifecycle product-owned and testable outside HTTP, keeping the route stable while lifecycle behavior moves behind TurnEngine and AgentEnginePort/RuntimeEngineContract.
Principle: route thinness is the design boundary; /api/harness/turn should validate, lock, forward to TurnEngine, write SSE, and clean up.
Runtime policy, engine invocation, event persistence ordering, and provider-specific behavior should not remain owned by the route.
Principle: Chirality terms own the public contract.
Public APIs, browser UIEvents, canonical HarnessEvents, session storage, permission decisions, and governance records must not become SDK-shaped except as adapter metadata.
Principle: the lock protects session semantics, not just code paths.

The requirement is one active turn per session with TURN_IN_PROGRESS on concurrent attempts; lock lifecycle stays tied to durable turn state and route cleanup so interrupted or failed paths cannot strand a session.
Principle: accepted-turn persistence is a reliance boundary.
Persist turn.accepted before SDK/model execution so killed or interrupted turns leave a recoverable record, verified by ordering tests rather than assumed from call structure.
Principle: SSE compatibility is not optional; browser event names remain stable during SDK adoption while internal mapping may become richer.
Principle: do not use this slice to widen capability; R1 preserves visible behavior and keeps write, bash, remote MCP, subagent, and domain-operation surfaces out of this deliverable.
